steps.step: Pin a model and effort to each agent (0.2.1)
Router: /mtk:go picks spec, chore or a develop mode and asks first (0.2.3)
Step 0: use mtk on a real task in Alta and list what went wrong
verify-gate: a chore cannot finish until verify.sh checked the files (0.2.4)
Memory: .mtk/ files, /mtk:handoff, stop after a commit and at 70% context (0.3.0)
Test memory in a restarted session, then commit and push 0.3.0
Decide whether /mtk:develop also needs the verify-gate
Lead + sessions: one lead opens real sessions with Herder or cmux
Self-learning on cron: read hooks/send.sh data and suggest PRs to improve mtk
Hook tests: tests/ feeds fake JSON to memory.sh, verify-gate.sh, strikes.sh, no-writes.sh, so verify.sh can check mtk itself
/mtk:doctor: check the installed plugin version matches the repo and that each hook really runs
Close the no-writes.sh hole: block reviewer writes by git state, not by a list of commands (python3 -c open() gets through today)
Optimize rule: every hook has a budget test (time, output size) and a review pass; fix STALE to look at all .mtk/ files
memory-checker agent: /mtk:handoff dispatches it before asking the user; it checks each .mtk/ line against git log, worktrees and the plan (read-only, sonnet)
spec-reviewer agent: checks a spec before the /mtk:spec gate — gaps, lines that cannot be checked, costs that break the user's limits
gate 4 risk check: flag plan steps that cost money, create cloud resources, or send data to an outside service
worktree cleanup in /mtk:doctor: list old mtk/* worktrees and branches and offer to delete them
